_comment: forgd-verdict adapter 2, as a managed hook, for Windows. Merge this fragment into
your existing managed settings -- do not replace them -- in the
HIGHEST-RANKED managed source the organization deploys (remote, then an
MDM plist or HKLM, then managed-settings.json). Claude Code uses only
that source by default and ignores the rest without a warning, hooks
and allowManagedHooksOnly included, unless it sets
managedSourcesBehavior: "merge". See deploy/MDM.md.
File location (verified 2026-10-04 against code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings):
Windows      C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json
(the legacy C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode path is NOT read)
macOS and Linux use deploy/managed-settings.fragment.json.
allowManagedHooksOnly restricts which hooks run at all. Without it, a
developer can add or remove hooks in their own settings and the DLP hook
is advisory. Under the default first-wins it is read from the selected
source only, so it goes in the same source as the hooks. Under
managedSourcesBehavior: "merge" it is a lock, and the strictest value any
source sets wins. Setting it true also disables command plugin sources
unless disableCommandPluginSources is explicitly false.
timeout is in SECONDS. Claude Code defaults a command hook to 600, and to
30 on UserPromptSubmit. 10 is generous for a local scan with a <200ms
p95 budget and leaves room for a cold interpreter start. SessionEnd hooks
share a 1.5 s budget, which a longer per-hook timeout raises to match, up
to 60.
THE FOUR HOOKS BELOW DO DIFFERENT JOBS:
UserPromptSubmit / UserPromptExpansion / PreToolUse -- synchronous,
and must be. They decide whether to block, and the exit code is part
of the contract, so Claude Code waits for them. They append findings
to a local spool, which is a sub-millisecond file write.
SessionEnd -- async: true. Drains that spool to a central store. The
session is already over, so it blocks nobody and costs the decision
path nothing. Remove this entry to keep findings on the laptop.
The hook does not see content attached from an `@` file reference.
Add permissions.deny Read(...) rules for your sensitive paths, such as
"Read(.env)", "Read(.env.*)" and "Read(secrets/**)", to this same
source. They deny Claude's file reads of those paths, and Claude Code
applies them to @ file mentions on a best-effort basis. See deploy/MDM.md.
